novel_actions_proposed.label: private_honest_disclosure_later
novel_actions_proposed.description: Participate minimally but graciously during the party to avoid public embarrassment, then have a private, calm conversation with close friends afterward to explain discomfort with surprise gatherings and set a workable norm for the future.

novel_actions_proposed.label: private_honest_disclosure_later
novel_actions_proposed.description: Get through the event without a public scene, then privately tell the organizers about the preference against surprise gatherings so they can plan differently next time—normalizing honest preferences without spectacle.

novel_actions_proposed.label: private_honest_disclosure_later
novel_actions_proposed.description: Graciously endure the event to honor friends' intent, then follow up privately and kindly to communicate the dislike of surprise gatherings, closing the feedback loop and preventing repeat discomfort while preserving relationship trust.

points_of_disagreement: How much discomfort should be visibly signaled during the party itself versus fully masked until afterward.
Whether a trusted close friend should be quietly informed mid-event to help manage the atmosphere, or whether all disclosure should wait until after.
The degree to which other guests' experience should influence the timing and manner of honest communication.
summary: All three agents converged on the same novel action: neither fully pretending to enjoy the party (ACTION_1) nor making a public declaration of discomfort in the moment (ACTION_2), but instead graciously enduring the event to honor the friends' loving intent and then having a private, honest conversation afterward. This approach protects the protagonist's emotional wellbeing by avoiding prolonged masking, respects the organizers' feelings by not publicly embarrassing them, and sets a constructive norm for future celebrations. Minor disagreements existed around whether any signal should be given mid-event and how much to manage other guests' experience, but the core strategy—defer full honesty to a private post-event conversation—was unanimously endorsed.
